items.name: Microcontroller
items.description: STM32N657X0 (Arm Cortex-M55) that executes all supervisor software and hosts the peripherals the system uses. Observable through the diagnostic serial line and the output pins.

items.name: Independent watchdog (IWDG)
items.description: Watchdog peripheral with its own clock and a 100 ms timeout; resets the microcontroller when not refreshed in time. Safety mechanism for faults the software cannot handle: after a detected fault the refresh is withheld, so a reset follows. Observable as an IWDG reset flag and, at the next start-up, a code 8 report with entity IWDG.

items.name: Window watchdog (WWDG)
items.description: Watchdog peripheral that resets the microcontroller when a refresh arrives earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous one. Safety mechanism for timing faults of the control cycle. Observable as a WWDG reset flag and, at the next start-up, a code 8 report with entity WWDG.

items.name: CRC peripheral
items.description: CRC unit that CON-SUP-003 lists as available. CON-SUP-003 establishes only its availability, not which CRC algorithms it supports, so no requirement is allocated to this element as the producer of CRC-32/MPEG-2 values (CON-SUP-129). The CRC value for the start-up and run-time integrity checks is produced by the software computation SYE-SUP-064 over interface SYE-SUP-065. This peripheral is unused for the integrity checks until a hardware source other than CON-SUP-003 confirms it can produce exactly the CRC-32/MPEG-2 value defined in SYE-SUP-065 (polynomial, initial value, bit order, final XOR); only then may it be used as an acceleration of SYE-SUP-064, through the HSI SYE-SUP-052, which therefore applies only under that condition (OP-SYE-002). Observable, when used, through the outcome of an integrity check (fault codes 5, 6, 7).

attributes.rationale: Finding F-sys-arch-item-r3-001: the item is split. The supported CRC computation is now the software element SYE-SUP-064 with its own interface SYE-SUP-065; this item represents only the peripheral, whose use is conditional on hardware evidence of capability (CON-SUP-003 states availability only). The conditional HSI SYE-SUP-052 now connects this peripheral and SYE-SUP-064 only (set-level finding F-sys-arch-set-r2-006).

items.name: CRC-32/MPEG-2 software computation
items.description: Computes the CRC-32/MPEG-2 value, as fully defined by CON-SUP-129, over the program code and the configuration block for the start-up integrity checks (SYS-SUP-016, SYS-SUP-018) and over the application range for the run-time check. For the run-time check it is responsible for the whole-image CRC (SYS-SUP-066): it carries the running CRC state from one segment to the next, so that at the end of each pass over the range __app_start to __app_end (segments per SYS-SUP-021) it has determined one CRC-32/MPEG-2 value over the whole range in increasing address order, not separate values per segment. Needs no hardware capability beyond the microcontroller. Observable through the outcome of an integrity check (fault codes 5, 6, 7).

items.name: CRC value (software computation)
items.description: Software interface by which the start-up and run-time integrity checks obtain the CRC-32/MPEG-2 value from the software computation. Start-up use: the start-up manager passes the whole checked range in one call and receives the final value (SYS-SUP-016, SYS-SUP-018). Run-time use: the run-time checker calls it once per control cycle with the next segment of __app_start..__app_end (SYS-SUP-021) in increasing address order; the computation keeps the running CRC state between calls, the state being initialised to 0xFFFFFFFF at the first segment of each pass and carried unchanged from one segment to the next, so that the value returned at the end of the last segment of a pass is one CRC over the whole range, not per-segment values (SYS-SUP-066). The next pass restarts at __app_start with the initial value. The value is valid only after the last segment of a pass; intermediate values are not compared. The work of each call (segment of at most 1 KiB plus the state update) is part of the run-time check budget of at most 0.5 ms processor time per control cycle (SYS-SUP-022). Observable through check outcomes.

attributes.data: start-up: whole range bytes in, CRC-32/MPEG-2 value out; run-time: one segment (at most 1 KiB, last segment shorter) in per call, running CRC state kept in the computation between calls, whole-image CRC value out after the last segment of a pass
attributes.range: polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR; bytes in increasing address order
attributes.timing: run-time: one call per control cycle (one segment per cycle, SYS-SUP-021); processor time of the run-time check at most 0.5 ms per control cycle (SYS-SUP-022); start-up: once before the application starts
attributes.error_behaviour: mismatch with the reference word -> fault code 5, 6 or 7; run-time state is not reset between segments within a pass
attributes.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r4-003: run-time segment interaction, CRC state preservation and timing added.

items.name: Timer (time base)
items.description: TIM peripheral that provides the time base of the timer-driven scheduler, the 100 us resolution measurement of start delay and execution time, the millisecond count since reset and the fault-free operating time. Observable through task release times and the time stamp of fault reports.

attributes.rationale: Independent of the supervised software for counting: fault-free time and millisecond counts come from this timer over SYE-SUP-053 to the fault manager and diagnostic communication.

items.name: Serial peripheral (USART)
items.description: USART that carries the diagnostic serial line at 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. Observable on the serial line.

items.name: GPIO
items.description: GPIO peripheral that drives the two control outputs and the status signal. From any reset until software configures them the pins are inputs; software then configures them as outputs driven low. Observable on the pins and, through the board, on the output levels.

items.name: Reset and clock control (RCC)
items.description: RCC peripheral that provides the clocks and the reset flags from which start-up classifies the reset cause as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, software or other. Observable through the RST start-up message.

items.name: Board output stage and pull-downs
items.description: Board part with an external pull-down resistor on each control output and on the status signal, holding them low from any reset until software configures them, and an output stage that takes at most 1 ms from pin change to output level. Observable by measuring the output levels.

items.name: Supervisor software
items.description: Aggregate of the supervisor software elements SYE-SUP-020 to SYE-SUP-029. Written in C11 without dynamic memory allocation or recursion, using at most 10 % of processor time over any 1 s window in normal operation, and runnable on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description and on host unit tests.

items.name: Start-up manager
items.description: Runs on the microcontroller after any reset. First configures the control outputs and the status signal as outputs driven low, then classifies the reset cause, transmits the RST start-up message and, only when the reset cause is classified as an independent or window watchdog reset (IWDG or WWDG), the code 8 report after the RST message (no code 8 report after a power-on, software or other reset), runs the start-up CRC checks of the program code and the configuration block using the CRC-32/MPEG-2 value from the software computation SYE-SUP-064 over interface SYE-SUP-065, starts alive supervision as soon as both checks have passed (SYS-SUP-009), without any further condition, withholds release of every supervised task until both pass and the safe-state latch is clear, and drives the status signal high (operational) only when the start-up integrity checks have passed, no fault has been detected since the last reset and the safe-state latch is not set (SYS-SUP-028); if a fault has been detected since reset, or the latch is set, the status signal stays low. Keeps the watchdogs from resetting a fault-free start-up (mechanism for the window watchdog is open in OP-SYS-002 and recorded as blocking OP-SYE-006). Observable through the RST line, the status pin and the first task release.

attributes.rationale: Finding F-sys-arch-item-r4-001: the start-up CRC checks obtain the CRC-32/MPEG-2 value through the software computation interface SYE-SUP-065 (element SYE-SUP-064), the chosen path for SYS-SUP-016 and SYS-SUP-018; SYE-SUP-052 is no longer listed here because it applies only conditionally to the CRC peripheral SYE-SUP-004 (OP-SYE-002), and any later hardware use is an acceleration of SYE-SUP-064, not a direct start-up manager connection. Sequence: outputs low, reset classification, RST message, code 8 report only if the reset is classified as IWDG or WWDG (SYS-SUP-034), integrity checks, release of tasks; status signal high only if checks passed, no fault detected since reset and latch clear (SYS-SUP-028).

items.name: Configuration and task scheduler
items.description: Reads the supervised task set (T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT at 10 ms and T_DIAG at 100 ms), periods, start limits (2 ms), execution limits (3 ms, 20 ms for T_DIAG) and release order from configuration data, validates it at start-up (fault code 9, latched safe state) and releases the tasks from the timer-driven scheduler in the configured order. Does not release any task while the safe-state latch is set. Observable through task release order and the fault code 9 report.

items.name: Timing supervision
items.description: Measures start delay and execution time of each supervised task with 100 us resolution and detects alive faults (code 1, no execution for 2 consecutive periods), late start (code 2) and overrun (code 3) within 100 us of the limit expiring; a value equal to the limit is within the limit. Safety mechanism. Fault detection: comparison against configured limits; reaction: notification to the fault manager. Observable through fault reports 1, 2 and 3.

items.name: Program flow supervision
items.description: At the end of each control cycle compares the checkpoints received from the tasks released in that cycle with the configured release order and detects a program flow fault (code 4) when they are missing or out of order; names the task expected at the first deviating position and signals one fault per control cycle. Safety mechanism. Observable through fault report 4 with its entity.

items.name: Run-time code integrity check
items.description: While the application runs, processes the program code range __app_start to __app_end (at most 1 MiB, excluding the byte at __app_end) one 1 KiB segment per control cycle in increasing address order, using at most 0.5 ms per cycle and completing a pass over 1 MiB within 11 s, and compares the whole-range CRC-32 with the stored reference (fault code 7, entity CODE). Safety mechanism. Observable through fault report 7 and the CPU budget.

items.name: Fault manager
items.description: Receives every fault detection, keeps a separate detection count per fault code (cleared after 60 s of fault-free OPERATIONAL time, and at a power-on reset), counts fault-free time without over-count, sets the safe-state latch at the third detection of a code (also for code 8) and at the first code 9, requests a software reset within 20 ms after a first or second detection of codes 1 to 7 once report and safe state are complete, never at the third, keeps the latch, counts and eight-entry fault history across software and watchdog resets, withholds watchdog servicing from the detection instant, and orders the safe-state entry and the fault report. Code 8 at start-up is counted but does not itself enter the safe state. Observable through the SW reset flag, the STS and GET FAULTS answers and the output levels.

attributes.rationale: No reset-retentive storage element is named by the inputs (CON-SUP-003 lists none), so none is allocated; the retained-state access interface SYE-SUP-067 is specified with its storage endpoint unresolved in the blocking open point OP-SYE-001. Fault-free time is counted from the time base over SYE-SUP-053 and status/history go to diagnostic communication over SYE-SUP-066.

items.name: Safe-state output control
items.description: Drives both control outputs and the status signal. Safety mechanism: on any detected fault it drives all three low within 49 ms of the instant the fault is detectable (board adds at most 1 ms, 50 ms total), holds them low while the latch is set (also after a software or watchdog reset), drives the status signal high only when the start-up checks passed, no fault was detected and the latch is clear. Observable on the three output levels.

items.name: Watchdog service
items.description: Refreshes the window watchdog once at the end of each control cycle and services the independent watchdog while every supervised task is healthy and no fault was detected since the last reset; stops both from the instant a fault is detected until the next reset; keeps both from resetting a fault-free start-up. Safety mechanism. Observable through absence of watchdog resets in fault-free operation and a reset after a detected fault.

attributes.rationale: Interference allocation (DEC-SYE-007, F-sys-arch-set-r2-004): this element is the only one that writes the IWDG and WWDG refresh through SYE-SUP-050 and SYE-SUP-051; the supervised tasks have no refresh interface (SYE-SUP-060 carries only release, start, completion and checkpoints), so a fault in an application task is not a source of watchdog refreshes. Its refresh decision depends only on supervision state held by the supervisor elements, not on data supplied by application tasks other than checkpoints.

items.name: Diagnostic communication
items.description: Sends the RST start-up message, fault reports FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> within 10 ms of detection (one per control cycle for code 4), except that a fault interrupted by a watchdog reset before its report and safe-state entry have completed needs no report and only the code 8 report at the next start-up applies, and answers the requests GET STATUS, GET FAULTS (the most recent eight reports, or all when fewer, made before the instant of request reception and since the last power-on reset, oldest first, one per line, then END, or only END when none; the qualifying history is fixed as of request reception, so a report made after that instant is transmitted as its own report between answer lines but is not a line of the answer and does not displace one of its eight reports) and GET RESET, ERR for unknown or over-long (more than 32 characters) lines, each accepted request (one received while no answer is being transmitted) within 50 ms measured from the received terminating line feed to the end of the last answer character, extended by the transmission time of the fault reports sent between the request and its answer; limits answer lines to 40 characters, never interrupts a line in transmission with a fault report (a fault report due during an answer line is sent after that line's line feed and before any further line of the answer), ignores a request received during an answer, and reports state STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE or LATCHED. Observable on the diagnostic serial line.

items.name: Fault-injection test hook
items.description: Present in test builds only; injects each fault class of fault codes 1 to 9. Absent from the production build (checked by inspection). Observable through the injected fault's report and reaction on the simulator or host.

items.name: Supervised application tasks
items.description: The cyclic application tasks T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT (10 ms) and T_DIAG (100 ms) that the supervisor releases and monitors; outside the supervisor boundary. They report checkpoints. Observable through checkpoint order and completion.

assumptions: A-INT-1: the tasks reach the supervisor only through SYE-SUP-060 and never write the watchdog peripherals, the GPIO control and status pins, or the supervisor's data (fault latch, counts, history, configuration, reference words)
A-INT-2: the tasks do not disable or mask the timer time base SYE-SUP-005 or the interrupts the scheduler depends on
attributes.rationale: Shared-resource interference (DEC-SYE-007, OP-SYE-008): A-INT-1 and A-INT-2 are allocated as system-level constraints on the application side of SYE-SUP-060; they are verified at system integration by fault injection of such accesses. DEC-SYE-008 makes them required protections, and the enforcement mechanism is not established: it needs the human decision recorded in the blocking OP-SYE-008.

items.name: Diagnostic tester
items.description: External system on the diagnostic serial line that receives start-up messages and fault reports and sends service requests. Observable as the counterpart of the serial line.

items.name: Controlled actuator and status consumer
items.description: External consumer of the two control outputs and the status signal; the safe state is defined by its inputs being low. Observable at the output levels.

items.name: Program image and configuration block
items.description: Memory regions defined by linker symbols: program code __app_start to __app_end (at most 1 MiB) with its reference CRC word at __app_crc, and configuration block __cfg_start to __cfg_end with reference word at __cfg_crc; end symbols are exclusive. Produced by the build, read by the supervisor. Observable by changing a byte and observing fault codes 5, 6 or 7.

items.name: Verification environment
items.description: Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description and host unit test tooling (gcc, gcovr) in which the supervisor is exercised without the real board (CON-SUP-005). CON-SUP-005 establishes only the platform and tooling; it does not establish which observation points the environment offers. The intended observations (GPIO output levels, bytes on the USART diagnostic line at 115200 8N1 per CON-SUP-007, and the RCC reset flags per CON-SUP-003) are therefore not claimed as capabilities here; each is a verification-environment need whose mechanism is recorded in OP-SYE-004 and settled by system integration verification.

attributes.rationale: Reset flags and USART/GPIO are peripherals named in CON-SUP-003, so the supervisor-side signals exist; whether Renode or the host tooling can stimulate and observe them is not stated in the inputs and is left as OP-SYE-004.

items.name: Independent watchdog refresh (HSI)
items.description: Hardware-software interface through which the watchdog service refreshes the IWDG; no refresh within 100 ms leads to a reset. Observable through the IWDG reset flag.

attributes.error_behaviour: no refresh -> IWDG reset; reset reason readable at start-up

items.name: Window watchdog refresh (HSI)
items.description: Hardware-software interface through which the watchdog service refreshes the WWDG once per control cycle. Observable through the WWDG reset flag.

attributes.range: refresh 6 ms to 12 ms after the previous refresh
attributes.error_behaviour: refresh too early or too late -> WWDG reset

items.name: CRC computation (HSI), conditional
items.description: Conditional hardware-software interface between the software computation SYE-SUP-064 and the CRC peripheral SYE-SUP-004. It applies only if a hardware source other than CON-SUP-003 confirms the peripheral produces exactly the CRC-32/MPEG-2 value (OP-SYE-002); until then the integrity checks obtain the CRC value through the software computation SYE-SUP-064 over interface SYE-SUP-065, and this interface is unused. If used, SYE-SUP-064 hands bytes to the peripheral over this interface as an acceleration, and the start-up manager and run-time checker still reach the CRC only through SYE-SUP-065; it is not a second path. Observable through check outcomes.

attributes.data: data bytes in, CRC-32/MPEG-2 value out
attributes.range: polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR
attributes.error_behaviour: mismatch with the reference word -> fault code 5, 6 or 7

items.name: Time base (HSI)
items.description: Hardware-software interface to the timer: time stamps for scheduling, 100 us measurements and milliseconds since reset. Observable through task timing and report time stamps.

attributes.data: time value, tick; to the fault manager the elapsed time used to count fault-free OPERATIONAL time (SYS-SUP-032, SYS-SUP-059); to diagnostic communication the millisecond count since reset for report time stamps (SYS-SUP-042)
attributes.range: resolution 100 us; millisecond count unsigned 32 bit, wraps after 4294967295 ms; fault-free time counted without over-count, the bound on under-count being that of SYS-SUP-032
attributes.timing: tick delivery to the fault manager at the 100 us resolution of SYS-SUP-085

items.name: Fault status and history (software)
items.description: Software interface by which the fault manager provides to diagnostic communication the state (STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE, LATCHED), the fault count since the last power-on reset and the eight-entry fault history used for GET STATUS and GET FAULTS answers. Observable through the STS and GET FAULTS answers.

attributes.data: state, fault count, history entries (code, entity, time stamp) most recent first
attributes.range: history of at most eight entries; reports made after the instant a request is received are not part of that request's answer (SYS-SUP-048, SYS-SUP-081)
attributes.timing: snapshot fixed as of request reception; answer within 50 ms per SYS-SUP-045

items.name: Retained fault state (software to retained storage)
items.description: Interface by which the fault manager stores and reads the safe-state latch, per-code detection counts and fault history so that they survive software and watchdog resets and are cleared at a power-on reset. Its storage-side endpoint is not identified because the inputs name no reset-retentive storage (OP-SYE-001); the microcontroller SYE-SUP-001 stands as endpoint until that decision is made. Observable by causing a software or watchdog reset and reading STS, GET FAULTS and the output levels afterwards.

attributes.data: latch, detection count per fault code, eight-entry fault history
attributes.range: survives software and watchdog resets; cleared at power-on reset
attributes.error_behaviour: not specified by inputs; see OP-SYE-001

items.name: Serial peripheral (HSI)
items.description: Hardware-software interface to the USART for transmit and receive of diagnostic lines. Observable on the serial line.

attributes.protocol: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit

items.name: GPIO pins (HSI)
items.description: Hardware-software interface to the pins of the two control outputs and the status signal: inputs from reset until configured, then outputs driven low. Observable on the pins.

attributes.timing: pins low within 49 ms of a detectable fault
attributes.error_behaviour: pins not configured -> inputs, board pull-downs hold low

items.name: Reset flags (HSI)
items.description: Hardware-software interface through which start-up reads the reset flags provided by the RCC after a watchdog, software or power-on reset. Observable through the RST message.

items.name: Reset path
items.description: Connection through which a software reset request or a watchdog timeout resets the microcontroller; retained state survives it except at power-on. Observable as a reset followed by the RST message.

attributes.timing: software reset request within 20 ms of the later of report completion and safe-state entry; independent watchdog path: reset when no refresh arrives within its 100 ms timeout (own clock, SYS-SUP-011); window watchdog path: reset when a refresh arrives earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous refresh (SYS-SUP-012); from fault detection no refresh is issued to either watchdog (SYS-SUP-010), so the independent watchdog's 100 ms timeout (SYS-SUP-011) bounds the time to reset; whether the window watchdog also resets on the absence of any refresh, and by when, is not established by SYS-SUP-012 and is recorded as OP-SYE-005, so no window-watchdog deadline for the no-refresh case is asserted here
attributes.error_behaviour: watchdog reset before both the report and safe-state entry have completed (including after the report has completed but before safe-state entry has completed) -> no report required for that fault, only code 8 at next start-up; retained state survives

items.name: Diagnostic serial line
items.description: Serial connection between the microcontroller and the tester carrying RST, FLT, STS and END lines and the requests GET STATUS, GET FAULTS and GET RESET. Observable at the line.

attributes.data: RST,<cause>; FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms>; STS,<state>,<fault count>; END; ERR; requests; lines end with line feed
attributes.range: RST <cause>: one of POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW, OTHER (SYS-SUP-037, SYS-SUP-038). FLT <code>: 1 alive, 2 late start, 3 overrun, 4 flow, 5 code integrity at start-up, 6 configuration integrity, 7 code integrity at run time, 8 watchdog reset, 9 configuration out of range (SYS-SUP-040). FLT <entity>: the task name for codes 1, 2 and 3, CODE for codes 5 and 7, CONFIG for codes 6 and 9 (SYS-SUP-040); for code 4 the task expected at the first differing or missing checkpoint (SYS-SUP-041); the entity for code 8 is IWDG or WWDG as stated in error_behaviour. FLT <ms>: unsigned 32 bit decimal number of milliseconds since the latest reset of any kind, 0 to 4294967295, wrapping to 0 after 4294967295, taken at the instant of fault detection and, for code 8, at the instant start-up classified the reset cause (SYS-SUP-042). STS <state>: one of STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE, LATCHED. STARTUP from any reset until the start-up checks pass while no fault has been detected since that reset and the latch is not set; a code 8 report at start-up leaves it at STARTUP (SYS-SUP-046). OPERATIONAL while supervising with start-up checks passed, no fault detected since the last reset and the latch not set (SYS-SUP-067). SAFE from the instant a fault is detected until the next reset while the latch is not set (SYS-SUP-068). LATCHED while the safe-state latch is set, regardless of any other state condition, so it takes priority over the other three (SYS-SUP-069). STS <fault count>: the number of fault reports since the last power-on reset, retained across software resets and watchdog resets (SYS-SUP-047); its textual number format is not specified by the cited requirements and is not asserted here. The STS answer itself (form STS,<state>,<fault count>, timing) is per SYS-SUP-045; ERR is per SYS-SUP-049.
attributes.protocol: ASCII lines, 115200 8N1; answer lines at most 40 characters, request lines at most 32 characters
attributes.timing: start-up RST message: transmitted within 10 ms of the instant start-up classified the reset cause (SYS-SUP-037); fault report within 10 ms of detection (the code 8 report at start-up likewise within 10 ms of the instant start-up classified the reset cause, after the RST message per SYS-SUP-090), except as stated in error_behaviour for a watchdog-interrupted fault; answer to an accepted request within 50 ms from receipt of the terminating line feed to the end of the last character of the answer, extended by the transmission time of the fault reports sent between the request and its answer (a fault report due before the first answer character precedes the answer; one due during an answer line follows that line's line feed and precedes any further answer line)
attributes.error_behaviour: unknown or over-long request -> ERR; request during an answer ignored; watchdog reset that interrupts handling of a fault before both its report and safe-state entry have completed -> the 10 ms fault report for that fault is not required, only the code 8 report (FLT,8,IWDG or WWDG) at the next start-up applies

items.name: Control outputs and status signal
items.description: Electrical connection from the GPIO pins through the board output stage to the controlled actuator and status consumer. Observable by measuring the levels.

attributes.data: two control outputs, one status signal
attributes.range: low = safe / not operational; high = operational for the status signal
attributes.timing: at most 1 ms from pin change to output level
attributes.error_behaviour: pin not driven -> pull-down holds low

items.name: Task release and checkpoint interface
items.description: Software interface by which the scheduler releases supervised tasks and the tasks report start, completion and checkpoints to the supervision elements. Observable through release order and checkpoints.

attributes.timing: per configured period and release order
attributes.error_behaviour: missing or late events -> fault codes 1 to 4

items.name: Image and configuration read access
items.description: Read access to the program image, the configuration block and their reference words by start-up, scheduler and run-time check. Observable through check outcomes.

attributes.data: bytes of regions __app_start..__app_end and __cfg_start..__cfg_end, reference words
attributes.range: end addresses exclusive; reference word 32 bit little-endian

items.name: Test hook interface
items.description: Test-build interface through which the verification environment injects faults of codes 1 to 9. Not present in production builds.

items.name: Fault notification interface
items.description: Software interface by which detecting elements signal a fault to the fault manager and by which the fault manager commands safe-state entry, watchdog withholding and reports. Observable through reports and outputs.

attributes.timing: safe-state outputs within 49 ms; report within 10 ms

decisions.text: Detection, fault counting, program-flow supervision and alive supervision are allocated to software; the final reaction to a fault relies on the hardware watchdogs by withholding refresh.
decisions.rationale: A software fault that stops the supervisor must still end in a reset (SYS-SUP-010, SYS-SUP-011, SYS-SUP-012).

decisions.text: The safe state is driven by software through GPIO and held at reset by board pull-downs; the 50 ms reaction budget is split 49 ms software and 1 ms board output stage.
decisions.rationale: SYS-SUP-025 and SYS-SUP-086 from CON-SUP-133; SYS-SUP-072 and CON-SUP-132 for the pre-configuration interval.

decisions.text: The supervisor is split into start-up manager, scheduler, timing supervision, flow supervision, run-time check, fault manager, safe-state output control, watchdog service, diagnostic communication and test hook, all running on the one microcontroller.
decisions.rationale: Each responsibility is separately observable for system integration tests; the single controller follows CON-SUP-001.

decisions.text: Fault reports take priority over answer lines at line boundaries, via the diagnostic communication element.
decisions.rationale: SYS-SUP-043 and SYS-SUP-074 require the report before further answer characters without interrupting a line.

decisions.text: The 10 % processor budget (SYS-SUP-052) covers the whole supervisor software; the run-time code check takes at most 0.5 ms per control cycle (SYS-SUP-022).
decisions.rationale: The 0.5 ms of a 10 ms cycle is 5 % of the 10 % total; the remainder is left to later stages.

decisions.text: Of the 10 % processor budget, 5 % (0.5 ms per 10 ms control cycle) is reserved for the run-time code check including the software CRC (SYE-SUP-024, SYE-SUP-064); the other 5 % is shared by all remaining supervisor elements (SYE-SUP-020 to SYE-SUP-023, SYE-SUP-025 to SYE-SUP-029) without a per-element split. Feasibility on the target is not shown because the inputs give no execution-speed or CRC-throughput figure for the software CRC; see OP-SYE-007.
decisions.rationale: SYS-SUP-022 and SYS-SUP-052; no measurement or platform datum is available at this stage, so no per-element figure is invented.

decisions.text: Independence assumption: the watchdog refresh is issued only by the watchdog service (SYE-SUP-027) after healthy supervision, and the IWDG runs on its own clock (SYE-SUP-002). A supervisor that stalls, or is starved by the application tasks on the same core, therefore stops issuing refreshes and the IWDG resets the microcontroller within its 100 ms timeout (SYS-SUP-011). Interference analysis over the shared processor, memory and data: (1) processor starvation or stall of the supervisor: no refresh is issued, so the IWDG on its own clock resets within 100 ms (SYS-SUP-011); (2) a faulty task issuing watchdog refreshes itself: excluded by assumption A-INT-1 on SYE-SUP-040, since SYE-SUP-027 is the only refresh source and SYE-SUP-060 has no refresh path; (3) corruption of supervisor data (latch, counts, history, configuration) or of the control and status pins by a faulty task: excluded by A-INT-1; corruption of the program image is detected by the run-time check SYE-SUP-024 (code 7) and the configuration block at start-up (code 6); (4) disabling the time base or scheduler interrupts: excluded by A-INT-2, and a stalled supervisor falls under (1). Whether the processor offers hardware memory protection, and how A-INT-1 and A-INT-2 are enforced (task priorities, memory protection), is a software-architecture decision recorded in OP-SYE-008; until it is made, A-INT-1 and A-INT-2 are assumptions that system integration tests exercise by injecting such accesses.
decisions.rationale: SYS-SUP-010, SYS-SUP-011 and DEC-SYE-001: the final reaction does not depend on the supervised software running; the allocation of the protections and assumptions answers F-sys-arch-set-r2-004.

decisions.text: Protection against interference (F-sys-arch-set-r3-004): A-INT-1 and A-INT-2 (SYE-SUP-040) are not accepted as mere assumptions. The architecture requires, as a system-level protection, that application tasks are prevented, by an enforcing mechanism and not by interface declaration alone, from (i) refreshing or reconfiguring IWDG and WWDG, (ii) driving or reconfiguring the control and status pins, (iii) disabling the time base or scheduler interrupts, and (iv) writing the fault latch, counts, history, configuration and reference words. Layers that exist without further hardware: the IWDG on its own clock resets a stalled or starved supervisor (SYS-SUP-011); the single refresh source SYE-SUP-027 reaches the watchdogs only after healthy supervision; image corruption is detected by SYE-SUP-024 (code 7) and configuration corruption at start-up (code 6). Not established: a mechanism that stops a faulty task writing peripherals or supervisor data, since the inputs name no memory-protection facility; this is the blocking open point OP-SYE-008, which needs a human decision. System integration verifies the property by injecting each of (i) to (iv) from an application task.
decisions.rationale: SYS-SUP-010, SYS-SUP-011, SYS-SUP-024, SYS-SUP-025: a faulty application must not be able to refresh a watchdog or corrupt supervision. No enforcement hardware is invented; the gap is recorded rather than hidden behind a deferral.

decisions.text: Allocation coverage (F-sys-arch-set-r3-006 to -089): every SYS-SUP and STK-SUP item named in those findings is an upstream source of at least one element of this architecture, as the findings themselves state ('allocated'). Those findings ask for a requirement or an open point, which is a requirement-set check (SQ-01) applied to the architecture stage; this stage writes no requirements. The only part of them that is a real gap, interference protection for STK-SUP-005, SYS-SUP-010 and the fault detection and reaction scenario, is addressed by DEC-SYE-008 and OP-SYE-008.
decisions.rationale: Trace coverage is decided by the deterministic trace gate; the architecture does not invent requirements.

open_points.text: The inputs do not name the storage that retains the safe-state latch, detection counts and fault history across software and watchdog resets (SYS-SUP-033); no reset-retentive hardware element is in CON-SUP-003, so none can be allocated or its reset and power-loss behaviour stated. Choosing the storage element (and its power-loss behaviour) is a hardware decision a person must make; the interface SYE-SUP-067 is specified without its storage endpoint until then.

Whether the CRC peripheral can be configured for CRC-32/MPEG-2 as required by SYS-SUP-016 is a hardware fact not stated in the inputs; the use of the peripheral or a software computation is left to the software architecture.
The pin assignment of the two control outputs and the status signal is not given in the inputs; it is needed for the GPIO configuration and the simulator platform description.

Blocking: whether the environment offers these observations and stimuli is a fact the architecture needs to claim verifiability (SYS-SUP-054) and the inputs do not state it. CON-SUP-005 names Renode with STM32N6 platform descriptions and host unit tests but does not state that the environment can observe GPIO output levels, capture the USART diagnostic line, read or inject the RCC reset flags (needed to exercise the watchdog and safe-state elements), or inject faults. The test-environment mechanism for each observation point (SYE-SUP-044) is decided and shown feasible by system integration verification.

SYS-SUP-012 states a reset for a refresh that arrives too early or too late; the inputs do not state whether the window watchdog also resets when no refresh arrives at all, nor the time by which it would. The reset path (SYE-SUP-057) therefore relies only on the independent watchdog timeout (SYS-SUP-011) for the no-refresh case; the window watchdog hardware behaviour is to be confirmed by the software architecture.

Start-up watchdog handling (SYS-SUP-015; upstream OP-SYS-002): the inputs do not state when the window watchdog is activated, its first-refresh deadline relative to reset release, or the duration of the start-up integrity checks, so a start-up sequence that keeps both watchdogs from resetting a fault-free start-up while the CRC checks run cannot be shown to meet the 100 ms IWDG timeout and the 6 ms to 12 ms window. A person must decide the activation point (for example, activating the window watchdog only after the start-up checks) and supply the platform evidence. Sequence otherwise per SYE-SUP-020: outputs low, reset classification, RST message, integrity checks, task release.

Processor budget feasibility (SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-052, SYS-SUP-058): no measurement or datum of the software CRC throughput or of the per-cycle cost of the other supervisor elements on the STM32N657X0 is in the inputs, so it is not shown that the 1 KiB segment CRC fits 0.5 ms per cycle, that a 1 MiB pass fits 11 s, or that all supervision fits 10 % over any 1 s window (DEC-SYE-006). Platform measurements or an accepted budget per element are needed.

Enforcement of isolation between the supervisor and the application tasks on the shared core (F-sys-arch-set-r3-004). DEC-SYE-008 requires, as a system-level protection, that application tasks cannot write the watchdog peripherals, the control and status pins, the timer time base or the supervisor data; an interface declaration alone does not give this. The inputs name no memory-protection or privilege-separation facility (CON-SUP-003 lists IWDG, WWDG, CRC, TIM, USART, GPIO, RCC only) and no statement of whether the application tasks are trusted. A person must decide either (a) that the target provides a hardware-enforced separation that the architecture may allocate, with the platform evidence, or (b) the accepted residual risk if the application tasks are treated as trusted. Until then A-INT-1 and A-INT-2 remain required properties whose enforcement is not established. Not deferred: the sw-arch stage cannot choose between (a) and (b).
